name: Launch film: what-if beats, three features, proof
suits: a product launch with a voice and no person on camera
a wish the viewer already has, then the product that grants it
three features in thirty seconds, each as one moving object

spine.note: The question the viewer already asks themselves, six words or fewer, the words climbing in from below with motion blur (kinetic-text entrance 'assemble'); the world's ground alone behind them, no product.

"What if ..." -- one wish per beat over the one object that stands for it (the customer as a silhouette, the conversation as a call pill); the object slides up under the words; the product still unnamed.
"Meet <product>": the wordmark lands big on the world with one accent (a sparkle, a ring); the voice says the name and nothing else.

The first feature as a checklist-toggles component: three to five rows (icon, label, switch) sliding into a stack, each switch flipping on as the voice names its row; one short line of type names the feature above it.

The second feature as a card-fan component: the group it works on (the people, the templates, the sources) as three to six cards spreading into a 3D arc and turning slowly; one short line of type names the feature.
The third feature on the product's real surface (a library mock), cut in full and held; one short line of type names the feature over its lower third.
The result on the product's surface with its numbers (a dashboard, a table with the winning row); the line names the outcome, a number stamps on it. Real figures only.
Back to the world's ground: the wordmark, the URL in a pill, a cursor clicking it; the voice says the ask in five words and stops.

type.note: one sentence per beat, the voice says it and the type shows its key words; type-card beats assemble word by word with motion blur, feature beats type on one line above the object

layers.world: one brand ground for the type beats (a sky, a color, a gradient) and a white product world for the feature and proof beats; every object has a floor shadow and a little perspective; nothing appears before the voice calls for it

asks.images: one object per wish beat (hero_image, in the film's palette)
asks.mockups: the product's real surface for the third feature and the proof
